text:
Alex: Observing steady memory growth on long-context runs when continuous batching is enabled. 2h job shows KV pages being reallocated frequently and throughput drops ~12%.
Priya: Can you paste profiler output? Sounds like page compaction or evictions thrashing.
Alex: Attached snippet:
```
mem_free: 120MB -> 40MB
kv_pages_alloc: 51200 -> 103200
page_faults/sec: 280
latency_p50: 14ms -> 21ms
```
Alex: Happens when many requests merge into a single batch (continuous batching) and we split downstream for different sequence lengths. Head-of-line blocking on large ctxs stalls small requests.
Dan: Reproduced locally. When batch-merge merges a long-context request at head, the KV cache tries to materialize huge KV slices; eviction kicks in and causes fragmentation.
Maya: Could be our page allocator's free-list fragmentation. How often do we compact? We only compact on full GC.
Priya: Profiling shows the "kv_lookup" hot path spending 35% time in memcopy after eviction. Before regression it was ~8%.
Alex: Perf regression started after kernel-selection change that favors grouped-attn kernels for long sequences. Might change memory layout.
Dan: Quick experiment: disable merge for requests with seq_len > 8k. rerun bench: benchbot shows:
```
# merge disabled for long ctx
throughput: +6% for small reqs
95p latency: -18% overall
memory_growth: -60MB over 1h
```
benchbot: CI perf run 1769447234 completed: baseline vs patch summarized above. diff attached.
Maya: Patch idea: mark large-kv ranges as "pin" to avoid eviction during merge, and aggressively reuse page-aligned slices instead of reallocating.
Priya: Also try switching to a segregated free list by size class to reduce fragmentation.
Alex: Sounds good. Dan can you prototype page pinning? I'll open a small A/B rollout on staging and monitor latency/evictions.
Dan: On it. Also adding a metric for "merge_orig_size" so we can detect when merging causes >X% extra kv materialization.
infra-bot: deploy/merge-pin-proto to staging started by Dan at 1769447401 :rocket:
Alex: Thanks, team. We'll regroup after a couple of runs. If staging looks good we can try kernel-selection rollback as a fallback.
